newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank of Thailand says baht has normalised.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Thailand says baht has normalised.

text.p: Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanonda said the baht had now returned to normal after being under pressure for some time.
Rerngchai told reporters late on Sunday that the central bank's Exchange Equalisation Fund (EEF) had bought dollars worth US$902 million between September 1 and 13.
The baht was sold heavily offshore on devaluation rumours between late July and early August and then again in early September, dealers said.
This forced the Bank of Thailand to intervene through offshore swap markets for the first time to defend the baht.
Rerngchai declined to reveal the total amount used in the intervention, but said the situation was now calm.
The Bank of Thailand's EEF sold dollars worth about US$770 million in July and a "small amount" in August, he added.
"So far, the amount of net capital outflows is not at a worrying level. And we keep monitoring the situation closely," he said.
Rerngchai also reiterated that the Bank of Thailand had no policy to devalue the baht, something the central bank has said many times to allay fears about the currency's future.
But he declined to comment on whether the Bank of Thailand planned to widen the dollar/baht trading band any time soon to make the currency more flexible.
The central bank now allows the baht to trade within a four-satang band, two satang on the down or upside, against the dollar.
The baht is pegged to a basket of major currencies.
